title: BMA executor workspace types
description: workspace.backup (machine-scoped executors) and the machine-token HTTP routes around it (contract 1.6.0, additive). Every route takes the machine credential as Authorization: Bearer <BMA_MACHINE_TOKEN>. Executor-domain path (ADR-0023 C.18) | legacy path: PUT /v1/machines/{machine_id}/backups/{backup_id}/archive | PUT /api/v1/daemon/machine-backups/{backup_id}/archive (request: application/octet-stream body = the archive, streamed, length may be unknown; header X-BMA-Backup-Fingerprint; 200 WorkspaceBackupArchiveStored; 409 when the backup is no longer uploading, a repeated upload included; 413 over the project's backup storage limit); GET /v1/machines/{machine_id}/backups/{backup_id}/archive | GET /api/v1/daemon/machine-backups/{backup_id}/archive (200 application/octet-stream, header X-BMA-File-Digest = digest; only a ready backup of the same machine); GET /v1/machines/{machine_id}/restore | GET /api/v1/daemon/machine-backup-restore (200 WorkspacePendingRestore, 204 nothing pending; read-only); POST /v1/machines/{machine_id}/backups/{backup_id}/restore/result | POST /api/v1/daemon/machine-backups/{backup_id}/restore-result (body WorkspaceRestoreReport, 204; 409 conflict when backup_id is not the machine's pending restore, which includes a repeat of an already recorded result, so an executor that retries after a lost answer treats 409 as recorded). The archive format is WorkspaceArchive.

WorkspaceBackupResult.description: workspace.backup result. digest and size_bytes describe the archive as the server stored it; skipped counts entries that could not be read (missing from the archive).

WorkspaceBackupArchiveStored.description: PUT …/archive 200 answer: the archive as the server stored it; the executor copies both into WorkspaceBackupResult.

digest.description: sha256 of the compressed archive bytes exactly as stored (not of the tar stream).

size_bytes.description: Length of the compressed archive in bytes.

WorkspacePendingRestore.description: GET …/restore 200 answer: the backup a recreated machine restores before executor.register. The executor downloads GET …/backups/{backup_id}/archive, checks length = size_bytes and sha256 = digest before writing anything, restores it (WorkspaceArchive), then posts the result. Failures are retried with backoff before registering; when giving up it posts state failed.

digest.description: sha256 of the compressed archive bytes exactly as stored (not of the tar stream).

size_bytes.description: Length of the compressed archive in bytes.

paths.description: Absolute roots the backup covered; only entries under them are restored.

WorkspaceRestoreReport.description: POST …/restore/result body. Unknown members are rejected (400). state restored also when some entries were skipped.

WorkspaceBackupFingerprint.description: X-BMA-Backup-Fingerprint and WorkspaceBackupResult.fingerprint: an opaque tree fingerprint (the reference executors use sha256:<hex>). The platform stores it and sends it back as skip_if_fingerprint; only equality with a value the same executor computed matters, so an executor may change the algorithm at the cost of one upload.

WorkspaceArchive.description: The archive bytes (no JSON). Format, as bmad 0.2.x writes it and bma-executor must read and write it: one zstd frame of a POSIX tar stream in PAX format (Go archive/tar FormatPAX: PaxHeaders.0 extended headers carry sub-second mtime, atime, ctime). Entries: for each path in paths, the path itself and everything below it in lexical walk order, minus exclude matches (an absolute exclude drops that path and its subtree; a relative one drops every entry whose base name equals it) and minus the executor's own BMA_HOME. Names are relative to / with no leading / or ./ (home/user/.bashrc); directory names end in /. Types: regular file (0), directory (5), symbolic link (2, target verbatim, absolute targets allowed); hard links, devices, FIFOs and sockets are not written (unreadable files neither; they count as skipped in WorkspaceBackupResult). Header fields: numeric uid/gid as on disk (root-owned entries stay 0:0), uname/gname empty, mode = permission bits only (0o7777), mtime. Restore rules (merge, never delete): an entry is written only if its cleaned name, read as /<name>, lies under one of WorkspacePendingRestore.paths, has no .. element, is not absolute, is a directory, regular file or symbolic link, and no existing parent on the way is a symbolic link; anything else is skipped and counted. Existing files are replaced, files not in the archive are kept, directories are created as needed. Ownership (numeric), permission bits and mtime are applied; atime and ctime are not restored. Symbolic links are created as recorded and never followed while restoring.
